item.title: New Border Numbers
item.description: The flood of illegal immigration into Texas has turned into a trickle. The head of Customs and Border Protection is out with new numbers. Commissioner Rodney Scott told Congress that there were around 90-thousand apprehensions along the southwest border last year. That, he says, was the same number they were catching each day under President Biden.

item.title: Data Center Water
item.description: Data centers are popping up all over Texas, and they’re using a ton of water. There is a concerns at the state legislature that the needs of high-tech firms would be placed ahead of both home owners are agriculture. State Representative Cody Harris led a hearing on it, today, in Austin. He says it’s a “difficult question” for lawmakers to balance. But he says we need to “ensure that future generations of Texas enjoy the Texas we enjoy now.”

item.title: Meat Packing Monopoly
item.description: President Trump wants to import meat from Argentina as a way to bring down beef prices. Ranchers are blasting the move, saying it’s a short term fix. Instead, they want the administration to address a monopoly of meat-packing companies. Texas cattle rancher Cole Bolton says that would be a long-term strategy to bring down meat prices at the grocery.

item.title: Murder For Hire
item.description: Five people in San Antonio, including three jail inmates, have been busted in what the cops are calling a murder-for-hire plot. Sheriff Javier Salazar says that surveillance of inmate phone calls uncovered the plans. One of the inmates, Adrian Farias, was reportedly trying to enlist other inmates to find somebody to kill a witness in his aggravated robbery case. There were also two people on the outside, involved.

item.title: Gun Sign Suit
item.description: A lawsuit challenging Texas’s handgun trespass signs is now being decided by the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. A church and a coffee shop claim that posting signs violates their first amendment rights. Their suit argues that they are uncomfortable giving oral notice or handing out written notice to each customer. The original lawsuit was filed in Houston back in 2020. Oral arguments were heard last month.
